scope: Bound aggregate IMAGEDEF plan staging and make the rvalue map transfer failure-atomic for caller payloads.

countedPayload: internal IMAGEDEF plan map node and entry object
definition common table-entry names, reactors, pending references, XDATA and application-data nodes/payloads
definition image name and reactor-map nodes/key/value strings
selected reactor vector slots and each reactor's common table-entry payload

behavior: Both const and rvalue plan setters run the aggregate estimate before validating/copying or consuming nested caller data; the existing 100,000-record cap remains in force.
The estimate includes dynamic DRW_TableEntry state for definitions and selected reactors, definition names and string-map entries, vector slots, and internal map-node storage.
Both setters keep the previously accepted plan unchanged on estimate, validation or allocation failure.

The rvalue setter first allocates every key/default map node, then performs only statically verified nothrow moves. Failure during a later node allocation therefore leaves every caller entry unchanged.

Focused controls cover exact logical byte acceptance, one-byte-over refusal, const map-node allocation failure, failure on the second rvalue map-node allocation, preserved prior plan/input, and corrected retry.

normalFocused.coverage: Existing definition/reactor count and full plan failure/retry/readback controls plus nested aggregate estimator boundaries and allocation-failure preservation/retry.

limitations: The byte estimate bounds logical retained payload/container slots; it does not measure allocator capacity or peak process RSS.
The internal ceilings are resource policy, not DXF format maxima or support claims.

The specific 100,001-entry IMAGEDEF plan-setter branch remains unexercised; the prior count receipt records the 100,001-slot OBJECTS inventory refusal. Other writeObjects maps/vectors, full-object rollback cases and the rooted IMAGEDEF TABLES/FIELDLIST failure remain open.
next: Continue auditing other writeObjects maps/vectors and setup/assembly bounds, including whole-object rollback after earlier staged records, source lifetime, platform numeric/string policies, scoped concurrency, and rooted IMAGEDEF TABLES/FIELDLIST failure.
